name: OAuth implicit flow
description:
The authorization server still honours the OAuth 2.0 implicit flow: a response_type=token (or id_token) request is answered with the access token in the redirect fragment. The token then sits in browser history, can leak through referrer headers and client-side scripts, and travels with no sender binding. The finding was proven from the captured exchange: the authorize request was answered 302 with a Location fragment carrying #access_token=.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's catalogue has no OAuth row; PortSwigger documents OAuth attacks as an Academy topic tested by hand.
remediation: Disable the implicit and hybrid grants on the authorization server. Use the authorization code flow with PKCE for every client type, including single-page applications and native apps.

references.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: OAuth authentication
